_note: Short tutorial cutscenes (scripts/ui/tutorial.gd). Each plays the first time its trigger event fires, when the room is free, and can be replayed from the pause menu. A step is one panel: speaker (principal, mentor or teacher), text (one or two short sentences, five lines at most), optional show (a pointer ring at podium, bell, noticeboard, cabinet, curriculum, teacher_desk, treat_shelf, desk:N or tile:X,Y) and optional demo (land, flash or puff, played on the pointed-at thing). Trigger names are fired by Game.fire_tutorial(). Prose only: no number stands in for a child's ability.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: In a lesson you can call a quick quiz. Stand at the podium and press Q.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: It costs a slice of the lesson clock. You can run it once a lesson.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: A child who is behind gets a blue bubble. Walk to that desk and press E to go over it.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: The class stays focused for the rest of the lesson. A quiz pays no grade, it only shows who needs you.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: That is homework in your arms. Take it to your own desk and press H.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Each sheet comes up as a page. Trace a check if the work is good, or an X if it is not.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: A check banks the sheet. An X does not.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Wave through a bad sheet and that child is marked as misjudged. A quiz can catch it later.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: You have taught a unit enough times to test it. The podium offers the test in the morning.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Hold E at the podium to start. It takes the day, and it cannot be sat twice.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Then you only watch, with no helping and no collecting. It tests the room you built.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Every result goes in the grade book on your desk. Press U to read it.

steps.speaker: mentor
steps.text: Press Z, or E at the alphabet poster, to open the lesson plans.

steps.speaker: mentor
steps.text: Each row is a lesson. In words, it tells you how well you know it.

steps.speaker: mentor
steps.text: Press E on a lesson to teach it next.

steps.speaker: mentor
steps.text: Later the Tab key lets you craft a lesson of your own.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: You have taught one subject often. A lesson in it can now be made Prestige.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Open the lesson plans with Z. On a lesson you have taught, press F.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: That lesson always deals a Legendary paper.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: A Legendary paper pays three times the coins and the experience. It never changes the grade.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: The cabinet is where everything you buy waits until you place it.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Press E on an item to take it out and place it in the room.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Press Left to sell one copy for half its price.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Room Ideas is the last tab of the shop. It shows ready-made layouts for your room.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Press Up and Down to browse. The picture shows where each piece goes.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Nothing is bought or moved. The count beside a name is how many of its pieces you own.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: The rooms you are closest to building come first.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: It is the last day. Before the bell, you choose what the final paper asks about.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Pick one lesson in each subject. The cursor starts on the lesson you taught most.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: Lessons you taught well lift the paper a little. Lessons you never taught pull it down.

steps.speaker: principal
steps.text: A child does a little better in the subject they love.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: A study folder sits on one desk. The child there can look things up.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: When they are stuck, they work it out themselves after a few seconds. No need to walk over.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: That earns them no experience, and it does not count as your help.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: It also stops that desk chatting and copying across to its neighbours.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: The grade book lies open on your desk. Press U to read it, at any time.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: It opens on the subjects page. Every lesson sits in its own subject column.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: A lesson you have taught is in colour, with the class's last letter beside it.

steps.speaker: teacher
steps.text: Press Tab for the register. It lists every lesson, unit test and exam you have given.
